title: Kayshon Boutte addresses trade rumors, future with Patriots
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Kayshon Boutte is linked to trade rumors amid a crowded Patriots' wide receiver room and upcoming roster decisions.
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel expressed openness to trading a receiver for the right price to manage roster depth.
Boutte focuses on current performance, ignoring trade whispers, aiming to impress ahead of a potential new contract.

title: Man charged after allegedly shoving 69-year-old woman at Nantucket ICE protest
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Lee M. Kennedy, 62, of Duxbury, charged with felony assault and misdemeanor disorderly conduct at Nantucket ICE protest.
Kennedy allegedly pushed a 69-year-old woman to the ground during a vigil and march on South Beach Street.
Incident caused public commotion; Kennedy's arraignment scheduled for September 8, no lawyer listed as of Thursday.

title: Critical Mass Boston to hold 15-mile bike ride in remembrance of cyclist struck and killed earlier this month
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Critical Mass Boston will hold a 15-mile remembrance bike ride for Louisa Gag on Friday, starting at Copley Square.
Louisa Gag, a Boston transportation planner, was fatally struck by a driver on July 9 on Tremont Street.
The event demands Mayor Wu enhance support for the Streets Cabinet to prevent future cycling tragedies.

title: This iconic 150-year-old tree was coming down in Belmont. These birds said, not so fast.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 150-year-old copper beech tree in Belmont was scheduled for removal due to disease-related deterioration.
Removal was delayed after discovering a protected nest of American robin nestlings in the tree.
The tree's removal has been postponed until the robins fledge, allowing residents more time to say goodbye.

title: A.J. Brown finally gets going, and other takeaways from Day 5 of Patriots training camp
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: A.J. Brown connects well with quarterback Drake Maye in Patriots' first padded practice of training camp.
Christian Gonzalez participates fully in practice despite ongoing contract negotiations with the Patriots.
DeAndre Hopkins concludes brief coaching stint with the Patriots during training camp as he considers his future.

title: Child on bike injured in crash with SUV in Wellesley
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: A child was injured in a bike-SUV crash at Oakland Street and Woodlawn Avenue in Wellesley on Thursday morning.
The child sustained potentially serious injuries and was transported to a Boston hospital for evaluation, police reported.
The SUV driver stayed at the scene and the Wellesley Police Crash Reconstruction Unit is investigating the crash.

title: Where to go in New England this August
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: The Milford Oyster Festival in Connecticut will run from August 14-15, featuring music, food, and local oysters.
The Foreside Inn, a new boutique hotel, has opened in Kittery, Maine, near shops and restaurants in Kittery Foreside.
Dine Out Boston event offers multi-course meals at participating restaurants from August 1-15, including three Saturdays.

title: Investigation underway after 2 found dead along same stretch of Mass. river
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two bodies were found less than a mile apart along the Connecticut River in Western Massachusetts.
Hermes Mariano Almonte, 21, drowned in Turners Falls, prompting an ongoing investigation with no foul play suspected.
Another unidentified male body was found near Smead Island; investigations by state and Montague police are ongoing.

title: Federal investigation finds Burlington schools violated the law over ‘graphic’ student survey
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Burlington Public Schools violated federal law by requiring students to take a survey with sensitive content against parental wishes.
The survey asked students about sexual activity and substance use, prompting parental complaints and a federal investigation.
The district must revise policies and provide an apology to affected families as part of the U.S. Department of Education resolution.

title: Pedestrian struck by vehicle on Cape Cod has died
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A pedestrian from Chatham died after being struck by a vehicle on Route 28 near Crosby Lane.
The incident took place in West Chatham around 7:50 a.m. last Saturday, with the driver staying on scene.
Chatham Police continue to investigate the crash; the pedestrian was airlifted and later succumbed to injuries.
